## Natural history notes

A native perennial climbing vine in the passionflower family, characterized by slender corky stems, small three-lobed leaves, and inconspicuous greenish-white flowers followed by small round berries. Corkystem Passionvine occurs in southern Florida, the Caribbean, and tropical America, where it grows in hammocks, thickets, woodland edges, and other partly shaded habitats. The vine climbs over surrounding vegetation using coiling tendrils and can form loose tangles along shrubs and small trees. Like other passionvines, it also serves as a larval host plant for several butterflies, including heliconians and fritillaries.
